transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose the thing that finally scared me enough to come in is that I’ve been having these mornings where I wake up and, before I’ve even really started the day, I find myself thinking it might just be easier if I hadn’t woken up at all. Not that I’ve made any plan to hurt myself—I haven’t—but the thought is there, and it’s unsettling.

I kept trying to tell myself it was just a bad morning or that I was being dramatic, but when it happens more than once, it starts to feel like something I shouldn’t just keep brushing aside. So… that’s why I’m here.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once looked forward to?

Yes… yes, I have noticed that. I still make myself go to things, because I’ve always believed that if you stop showing up, it gets harder and harder to start again. So I’ll go to my book club, and I’ll sit there with everyone talking about the chapter or who liked which character, and I’m nodding and making the right little comments, but it feels like I’m sort of… behind a pane of glass. Like I can see everyone enjoying themselves, but I can’t quite get to where they are.

And there’s a dance night I used to look forward to—nothing fancy, just a community thing—and I still go sometimes because I don’t want to become someone who just stays home all the time. But it doesn’t give me that spark anymore. I’m there, technically, but I’m not really in it.

Even at home, the things that used to reliably make me feel a bit lighter don’t do much lately. My garden, for instance—I used to get such satisfaction from tending it, noticing what was blooming, fussing over the herbs. And I like cooking for my neighbors; that used to give me a real little lift, you know, making something and bringing it over. Lately I can still do it, but it feels more like I’m going through the motions than actually enjoying it.
How often have you felt down or depressed most days, and how long have these feelings been happening?

It’s been… about a month now, I think. Not just a bad day here and there, but most days, yes. It started after my sister died unexpectedly, and I suppose at first I told myself, “Well, of course you feel awful, anyone would.” And that’s true, I know that’s true.

But it hasn’t really lifted the way I kept expecting it to. I wake up with it, or it settles over me sometime during the day, and it’s been there more often than not since then. So… yes, about a month. Since she died.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep—like trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or sleeping much more than usual—nearly every day?

Yes… my sleep has been off, pretty much every night. I can usually get to sleep at first, but it doesn’t feel like proper sleep, if that makes sense. It’s more like I fall asleep in little bits and pieces, and then I’m awake again, and then I drift off, and then I’m awake again.

The worst part is the early morning. I’ll wake up before dawn, when it’s still dark, and my mind is already going. It’s not a gentle waking-up, it’s like I come to and everything is already turning over in my head. And once that starts, I usually can’t settle back down. I’ll lie there trying to be still, telling myself I should rest even if I’m not sleeping, but the day feels like it has already started before it’s supposed to.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or maybe feeling restless and unable to sit still, especially when you're not trying to be calm or relaxed?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I’ve noticed anything dramatic that way. I’m not pacing the house or wringing my hands or anything like that, at least not that I’m aware of.

As for moving slowly… maybe I feel slower inside, if that makes sense, but I don’t know if anyone watching me would say I’m actually moving slowly. I still get up, make tea, do the ordinary things. Sometimes I’m less efficient, I suppose, but I haven’t really thought of it as my body being slowed down.

So… no, I don’t think that’s been a big thing for me. Or if it is, I haven’t noticed it clearly.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yes… I have noticed that. I wouldn’t say I’m deliberately dieting or anything like that, not at all. It’s more that food just doesn’t seem to… call to me anymore, if that makes sense.

I’ll think, oh, I should eat something, and then I’ll make a piece of toast, or heat up a little soup, something easy. But it feels more like I’m doing it because I know people are supposed to eat, not because I’m hungry or looking forward to it. And then evening comes and I realize I’ve barely had anything all day. It surprises me sometimes, because I used to structure the day a bit around meals, you know, even simple ones.

As for weight, I haven’t been trying to lose any. I’m not making some effort in that direction. But with eating less like that, I suppose it wouldn’t shock me if I had lost a little. I just haven’t been paying very close attention.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you’re not worth much lately?

Yes… yes, I think I have. It’s mostly tied up with my sister. I keep going back over those last weeks in my head, over and over, like I’m trying to find the moment where I should have done something differently.

I tell myself I should have called more often, or stayed on the phone longer when I did call, or listened better instead of saying the usual things. Sometimes I think maybe I should have asked different questions, or noticed something in her voice, or been more useful somehow. And then another part of me knows, at least logically, that I probably couldn’t have changed what happened. I know that. But it doesn’t seem to stop the feeling.

It’s not always a clear thought like “this is my fault,” exactly. It’s more this dull, nagging sense that I didn’t do enough, that I fell short somehow. And I keep replaying little conversations, wondering if I was distracted, or if I missed chances to be kinder. It makes me feel… not worthless in a dramatic way, but like I wasn’t the sister I should have been. Like I should have been better.
Would you say that your thoughts have been slowed down or that it's harder to get yourself moving during the day, even when you know you should be doing something?

Yes… more the getting myself moving than my thoughts, I think. I don’t know that my thoughts are slowed exactly, but my body feels… heavy. Like there’s a delay between knowing what I need to do and actually being able to make myself do it.

Even simple things can take so much out of me. I’ll have one small errand to run, something that shouldn’t be a project at all, and by the time I’ve done it I feel worn out, as if I’ve done far more than I actually have. Or I’ll sit down to get papers together for the Cultural Center — just sorting, putting things in order, nothing physically demanding — and somehow it feels like my whole body is moving through thick mud.

It’s frustrating because I can look at the task and know it’s ordinary. I know it shouldn’t be such a big effort. But then I’m sitting there staring at the papers or standing with my coat in my hand, trying to gather enough energy to just begin. And once I do begin, I tire so quickly. It makes everything feel harder than it ought to.
Have you noticed that your movements have been slower than usual, or that it takes you longer to get started with things physically, even when you know what you need to do?

Yes… yes, I think that’s fair to say. It’s not that I’m completely unable to move or anything, but everything feels slower to start. I can know perfectly well what I need to do — put on my shoes, take something to the post office, gather up the papers for the Cultural Center — and still I just sort of… sit there, as if my body hasn’t caught up with the instruction.

Even the small things feel strangely heavy. A simple errand can leave me worn out, much more than it ought to. And with the Cultural Center papers, it’s not as though they’re heavy boxes or anything — it’s just sorting and putting things together — but I find myself moving so slowly, like I’m pushing through thick mud. I’ll look at the stack and think, all right, start with this one folder, and even that feels like an effort.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I know these are ordinary tasks. They shouldn’t take that much out of me. But lately it feels like my body tires before I’ve really done much at all.
